nc-commissioner-districts.summary: Every North Carolina county is run by an elected board of commissioners. The County card names its members, but this app does not show you which commissioner district you live in, so it cannot say which member is yours.
nc-commissioner-districts.why: No statewide map of commissioner districts is published, and state law keeps each county's district lines in the county clerk's office as a written description rather than as a map.
nc-commissioner-districts.wanted: Each county's current commissioner district boundary, as a downloadable file or a public map service from the county's own GIS office.

nc-conservation-boards.concept: Soil and water conservation district board
nc-conservation-boards.summary: The County card names your soil and water conservation district's supervisors from the state's directory. Some seats are listed there with no name, and a seat that changed hands since it was printed may show the earlier supervisor.
nc-conservation-boards.why: The state's only list of who holds these seats is a directory printed from a database the public cannot search, and it lists some seats with no name and nothing to say whether they are vacant.
nc-conservation-boards.wanted: A list of every district's supervisors that the state keeps current and publishes as data, saying which seats are vacant and when each one last changed hands.

nc-municipal-officeholders.summary: This app names the mayor and council of North Carolina's 42 cities and towns above 25,000 people, and not those of its 510 smaller cities, towns and villages.
nc-municipal-officeholders.why: No state office publishes who holds North Carolina's city offices or where their council districts run, so each of the 42 is read from its own pages, and the districts of the 17 that elect by district from each city's or county's own map.
nc-municipal-officeholders.wanted: A statewide list of every city, town and village's mayor and council, kept current, saying which seats each district elects and which the whole place elects, and a statewide map of council districts kept as current as the places' own.

nc-school-board-districts.area: North Carolina — the 38 school boards that elect members by district
nc-school-board-districts.summary: Where a school board elects members by district, this map draws the districts from election results, so some places show two or more districts and parts of a few school districts show none.
nc-school-board-districts.why: No published map of these districts has been found. Each is drawn from the precincts that voted in its seat's latest election, and where a line runs through a precinct, or a seat was not on the ballot lately, the results cannot place it.
nc-school-board-districts.wanted: Each board's election district map, or the list of precincts each of its districts contains, published by the State Board of Elections or by the board itself.

nc-school-board-members.summary: This app names your school district and, where its board elects members by district, draws your district, but it names nobody on the board.
nc-school-board-members.why: No statewide list of who sits on each school board now has been found. The State Board of Elections' results name each election's winners but not a member appointed since, so the app names nobody rather than a winner who may have left.
nc-school-board-members.wanted: A statewide list of who sits on each school board now, or each district's own published list of its board.

nc-tribal-government.summary: The Tribal Government card draws the Qualla Boundary and its trust land, and names the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians and the communities the Census draws on that land. It does not name anyone on the Band's council.
nc-tribal-government.why: The Band's website could not be read from where this project is built, because its security certificate could not be checked. Whether the fault is the site's or this connection's is not settled.
nc-tribal-government.wanted: The Band's own council list, read from a machine that can check the site's certificate.
